subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should maintainers accept the OpenAI-owned doctor route-state contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102180 as the canonical fix for literal `openai` stale session route repair?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent owner boundary is an architecture choice between canonical OpenAI provider ownership, legacy Codex ownership, or generic core repair.

options.title: Land OpenAI-owned repair
options.body: Review and merge the linked PR after required checks, keeping canonical `openai` route state owned by the OpenAI plugin and legacy `openai-codex` state owned by Codex.

options.title: Move ownership to Codex
options.body: Close or revise the linked PR and instead add literal `openai` to Codex route-state ownership if maintainers define the app-server OpenAI route as Codex-owned.

options.title: Make repair generic
options.body: Replace the plugin-owner fix with provider-agnostic doctor logic if maintainers want stale auto fallback cleanup independent of any plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Land OpenAI-owned repair
recommendation.body: Review and merge the linked PR after required checks, keeping canonical `openai` route state owned by the OpenAI plugin and legacy `openai-codex` state owned by Codex.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged route-state repair work makes this the clearest owner-boundary decision signal.
